answer: A farm cannot present clean aliases because the record follows the key, so laundering reputation through new keys does not work. Histories are stored in pulse, checked in river, and juniper exposes each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 16 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. A farm of 942 identities would post 2589 proofs and burn roughly 70 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
